A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Understanding Fixed Predictions via Confined Regions. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–G are available and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on three datasets, region-enumeration and distribution-shift analyses, and a Pennsylvania sentencing-risk audit.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4–5 and Appendices E–G.

M1.justification: The ReVer procedure is unchanged: MIQCP optimization using Farkas certificates, treatment of discrete variables through continuous restrictions, and sequential box enumeration using no-good cuts.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate heloc, givemecredit, and twitterbot, retain the Pennsylvania SRAI case study, and examine the same distribution-shift scenario in Appendix F.

E2.justification: Tables 3 and 7 retain the same Data, Region, and Score comparators against ReVer. Appendix F retains its comparison involving the Data baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain the 50% training split, cross-validated regularized logistic regression, region-selection rules, 100-point Region sampling, and identical evaluation metrics. The box-enumeration and distribution-shift protocols also match.

E4.justification: The box-coverage analysis in Figure 2, distribution-shift analysis in Appendix F, and sentencing-risk case study are retained without substantive changes. No ablations or supplementary analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Table 7's computation-time summaries and parenthetical quantities. No additional run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: Tables 3 and 7 contain identical results, including ReVer's average runtimes of 4.67, 0.13, and 0.07 seconds. Figures 2–3 and the SRAI findings—fixed predictions for individuals under 21 and males aged 21–25—also match.

T1.justification: Figure 1 changes the illustrative classifier from 1[x1 + 10x2 ≥ 20] to 1[x1 + 10x2 > 20], altering its boundary condition. The formal optimization formulations, assumptions, theorems, and appendix proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution now explicitly restrict the verification method to linear classifiers, making the headline scope more precise. This aligns with the restriction already present in v1's technical sections; the central contributions and guarantees are retained.

C2.justification: The introduction adds an explicit qualification that pointwise auditing without available data requires synthetic samples that may not represent the full population. Interpretations of the empirical results and the existing limitations concerning linear models and box expressiveness remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same code location, Python implementation, Gurobi 9.0 with default settings, Apple M1 Pro hardware with 32 GB RAM, and detailed actionability constraints in the appendices.

R1.justification: The same 48 references and substantive comparisons with prior recourse research are retained. Although repeated 'first method' wording is removed, both retain the positioning that prior work does not characterize confined regions; citation-style changes are presentational.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten and the introduction reorganized around pointwise auditing and data availability. Other edits reduce emphasis on the ReVer name, refine wording, and add a generic Impact Statement; the main section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables. Figure 1 and its caption are revised, Table 2's rows are reordered, and the case-study illustration moves onto a separate page from its introduction.

improvement.justification: v2 states the linear-classifier scope more clearly in its headline claims and better explains the data requirements of pointwise auditing. These provide modest gains in precision and accessibility while preserving the method, proofs, and empirical evidence.
